summary: Client-side protocol flip during reconnect causes suppressed postamble (final paragraph) in resumed SSE stream
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that after a transient network redirect during an SSE session resume, the final paragraph (postamble) is missing from the resumed response. Impact: user-visible truncation of generated content for some resumed sessions; reproduces intermittently behind CDN/proxy path changes. Environment: production; NotaDocs uses the hosted API via a corporate CDN in front of Redwood's edge.

Observed behavior: when the customer's browser experiences a protocol flip on reconnect (HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 via CDN rebind) the client receives a resumed stream that contains all earlier chunks but the concluding paragraph is absent and there is no explicit "end" event. Expected behavior: resume emits the remainder of tokens and a terminal end event (or consistent event-id) so the client can reassemble and finish rendering the response.

Notes: ticket opened from customer support escalation (CSR). They provided HAR traces, server request IDs, and a short video showing the final paragraph missing after an automatic reconnect following a 307 redirect from the CDN.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Client opens SSE stream to /v1/streams with resume token enabled behind corporate CDN (example path uses HTTP/2 to CDN -> backend HTTP/1.1).
2) Mid-generation, induce a network redirect (simulate CDN rebind / 307) forcing the client to reconnect and resume using last-known resume_token and last-event-id.
3) Observe the resumed stream: payload arrives but concluding paragraph (last ~150 tokens) is missing; no final 'end' event present.
4) Repeat with websocket fallback — websocket resumes and completes normally (serves as workaround).
logs: customer_har_excerpt: request id c3f9-2487, upstream id=us-east-edge-12, resume_token=rt_9a3f, last_event_id=evt_4432
edge_log: 2026-03-09T18:12:04Z REQ c3f9-2487 -> backend-uplink (h1) negotiated tracing; noticed transfer-encoding: chunked -> proxy transformed into http/1.1 with keep-alive rewrite
serving-runtime: 2026-03-09T18:12:04Z STREAM resumption requested token=rt_9a3f seq=4433; writing tail buffer (final chunk) and issuing terminal event id evt_4433
client console: Event id seen twice (evt_4432) and dedupe logic suppressed content tagged without incremented event id
cdn_debug: fastly rule applied 307 rebind -> re-sliced connection; content-length/keep-alive munging observed in some cases
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): verified customer HAR and repro steps, reproduced in lab behind similar CDN configuration using Fastly managed service.

Hypothesis: client deduping uses last_event_id and will ignore events with same id; during protocol flip the edge rewrites/merges the final chunk causing resume sequence number to not advance in some code paths, so final event appears 'already seen' to client and is dropped by the SDK.

Evidence: serving-runtime logs show terminal event emitted with new id evt_4433, but client-visible stream contained evt_4432 as last ID. Edge logs indicate chunk coalescing and header rewrite between h2 <-> h1 causing the terminal event payload to be appended to a keepalive frame that the client replays in a way that duplicates the previous event id header parsing path.
SRE reproduction: created a synthetic test that forces H2->H1 rebind on resume; failure reproduced ~40% of the time with configuration that mirrors customer's CDN rules. Websocket path unaffected.
Intersection with SDK: Redwood JS SDK dedupe code suppresses messages with non-incrementing event ids; this behavior combined with edge coalescing resulted in the final event being ignored.
Risk assessment: P1 for enterprise customer with partial content loss; impacts a subset of resumed sessions only (dependent on CDN path and timing).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 - Priya Patel (Support): Aisha provided HAR and video; I reproduced locally using a curl pipeline with HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 proxy and saw the same missing terminal paragraph. Moving to In Progress and looping in Edge SRE.

2026-03-10 13:02 - Diego Morales (SRE): Confirmed edge logs show chunk coalescing during rebind. Fastly config showing rule fs-redirect-serve that performs proxy handoff. Created a short repro harness and pushed to staging for debug.

2026-03-11 08:45 - Marcus Li (Eng): Found that the serving-runtime emits terminal event with id increment, but the edge can replay the previous event-id line in certain chunking combinations. Opening PR to add explicit terminal sentinel header 'X-Stream-End: 1' so edge preserves finality semantics across protocol transitions. See PR link below.

2026-03-11 15:20 - Customer (NotaDocs): Confirmed websocket fallback completes reliably; they can apply workaround but prefer SSE fix since they rely on SSE for integration with their content pipeline.

2026-03-12 10:05 - Marcus Li (Eng): Deployed edge-side patch to staging that prevents coalescing of final chunk when resume token present; working on production rollout plan (gradual by region) and publishing SDK advisory to add event-id monotonicity check tolerance for +1 vs. repeated id within a 500ms window.
Slack: #support thread SUP-707707 with logs and staging link: https://slack.redwood-internal/archives/C0123XYZ
resolution: Mitigation and rollout plan: 1) Immediate customer workaround documented: use websocket fallback or ask CDN to disable aggressive HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 rebind rules for streaming endpoints. 2) Short-term fix: SDK advisory released to tolerate a single non-incrementing event id within a 500ms window during resume to avoid suppression of terminal payloads (patch released to JS SDK v2.4.1). 3) Edge/server fix: deployed patch to edge that preserves terminal chunk boundaries when resume_token present and adds X-Stream-End header; will do phased rollout to prod us-east on 2026-03-13 followed by eu-west. 4) Postmortem/Follow-up: one UX follow-up to add server-side watchdog that re-sends terminal event if streaming session doesn't close within 2s of last token; track as follow-up action item in confluence page above. Status: fix in staging, targeted prod rollout 2026-03-13.
notes_for_followup: After prod rollout, confirm with NotaDocs that resumed sessions succeed for at least 48h under similar CDN conditions. Consider permanent protocol-conversion hardening on edge and add test harness to CI that simulates H2->H1 rebind during resume.
